Stochastic 2026

sLLM: the summer record

sLLM pairs a slime mould with a language model, although this project is not really about either of them. It is a study in how to interface two very different kinds of systems.

The question

A study of two disparate systems

This work is less about a language model and a slime mould specifically than about how they interface: how they come into contact, what that contact does to what each produces, and how they shape each other's output.

Every interface is a reduction. What crosses it, and in what form, is the main thing being designed. The organism reaches the model as four numbers: period, amplitude, the phase lag between electrodes, baseline drift. The model reaches the organism as light in one region of the chamber. Nothing else crosses in either direction, and everything the work claims has to survive that narrowing.

There is a reason for this pair. Neither system has a part inside it that is in charge. Physarum is one cell with no nervous system: different parts of it contract slightly out of step with each other, and the direction it moves is a consequence of that timing. A language model has no single place where meaning is stored. It is a large set of numbers, and every word it produces comes from all of them at once.

Whether the model and the organism can entrain one another is what the whole project is working toward.

The seven prompt variants

They differ only in what the model is told it is coupled to. The loop, the action and the state format are the same in all seven.

BLIND

The default. The model is given the interface and nothing else, and is never told what it is coupled to.

INFORMED

The same interface, plus the name of the organism. The difference from BLIND is what the model's priors about Physarum contribute.

CYCLES

The period is withheld. The model has to estimate it, and every duration it sets is converted using its own estimate.

ADVERSARIAL

The organism's activity consumes the model's context. Quiet turns cost less, and blue light quiets the organism.

METERED

The organism's period sets the model's memory budget. Shorter period, more context. What light does to the period is not stated.

MIMIC

Physarum's architecture rather than its vocabulary. No history, a decaying trail on the surface instead, changes rather than values, no note.

NULL

BLIND with the task removed. If the notes still claim influence, the claim is coming from the format and not from the data.

In plain language

What is in the dish, and what the wires are doing

Four small blocks of agar sit in a petri dish. A metal probe runs into each one. Three of them are measuring probes; the fourth is the reference, the point everything else is measured against.

A chip reads the voltage of each measuring probe against the reference, once a second, and writes it to a file. A camera photographs the dish every few minutes. Nothing else is required to make a recording.

The slime mould is placed on the reference block. It has no nervous system and no central point where anything is decided. It is one cell that spreads, and it explores by pushing tubes of itself outward. When a tube arrives at one of the measuring blocks it connects that probe to the reference through its own body. Only then is there anything to measure at that site.

So the organism decides, by growing, which of the three channels become live and when. That is the whole experiment: the dish is wired in advance, and the connection is made by an organism rather than by hand.

/drift

The system hosted on a Raspberry Pi

A complete system on one Raspberry Pi in a sealed chamber: sensing, actuation, recording, a local model, a web layer for remote control and for visitors, and an audiovisual presentation layer.

Sensors

  • Electrodes. Three measuring plus a reference, in agar islands, read against the reference once a second by a 16-bit converter at 8 samples per second.
  • Temperature and humidity. Logged at 1 Hz, so the chamber itself can be ruled out as the source of anything found in the electrode record.
  • Camera. Timelapse, for documentation and for dating precisely when a tube reaches an island.

Actuators

  • LED matrix, nine zones. The only thing the model can change, and the lever for the blue-light stimulus test.
  • Fan. Relay plus PWM, for the chamber.

Host and web layer

  • Livestream of the dish.
  • Graphs of the raw electrode signal and of the reduced slime-mould signal.
  • Model logs : what it asked for, what was applied.
  • Admin panel for changing experiment parameters remotely.
  • Archive, so a visitor can go through past runs themselves.

/drift, the presentation layer

The audiovisual piece. A visitor can slide a window over the historical record and set the playback rate. Playback rate is a compositional decision, not a setting: at real time the causal link between image and sound is imperceptible, and compressed too far the two collapse into simultaneity and the asymmetry is lost.

/drift is for one thing: approximating, for a visitor, the feeling of a vein contracting and expanding. That rhythmic cycling of expansion and contraction is found throughout life itself.

Status of the loop

The light and the signal have never once overlapped. The last light event logged was 2026-08-22 06:14 CEST; the first electrode was bridged 2026-08-24. Every phase-lock window since contains zero light onsets, which is why that analysis has never rendered a result: it reports "insufficient" rather than a negative, by design. The entrainment question is untested, not answered.

The finding 2.2–2.4 min
0.5–1.8 mV
p < 0.005

A rhythm that appears only where the organism has arrived

Every probe the organism reached began to rise and fall on a cycle of roughly two minutes, by up to 1.8 thousandths of a volt. Probes it never reached did not. Neither did the hours before it arrived.

A recording always wiggles somewhat, at every speed. The claim here is not that there is movement in the trace. The claim is that there is about ten times more movement at one particular speed than at the speeds immediately either side of it. That bump is the finding, and it is the only thing the statistics are asked about.

The same dish, with and without the organism

A rhythm in a recording can come from the room, the instrument, or the agar. The test for that is to take the organism out and leave everything else alone. Run 7 and run 8 were exactly this, back to back: the same dish, the same agar blocks, the same probes, a day empty, then the organism returned to the same blocks, then removed again.

Tube retraction, 2026-08-26

On 2026-08-26 at 04:05 a tube let go of one probe and pulled back, while the tube on the other probe stayed put. Nobody arranged this. It switched one site off and left a control running in the same dish, in the same hours.

Limitations

What the evidence does not establish

The rhythm requires the organism. That much is established. What it does not establish is that the rhythm is the organism.

Two explanations survive every measurement so far. One is the organism's own electrical activity. The other is chemistry at the metal surface, where the body of the organism is pressed against the probe. Taking the organism out removes both at once, so the removal test cannot separate them.

The test that can is stimulus and response: change something the organism cares about while it stays connected, and see whether the rhythm changes with it. Blue light is the lever, because P. polycephalum registers blue and near-UV, and a metal surface has no reason to. That run is written down in full: blocks, timings, statistic, decision rule and the conditions that would void it, and is waiting on the light panel, which condensation in the chamber has twice destroyed.

Limitations

n = 1. One dish, one organism, two colonization events, one rig. Nothing here is replicated. Whiting et al. put the base rate for this assay at roughly ten usable dishes in twenty, and 42 of 240 single-tube dishes producing the oscillations being looked for.

The slow rhythm is missing. The rig was designed around a 30–40 minute band reported at 4–5 mV. It measures 0.23–0.47 mV here, ten times under. It is not expected to appear.

Agreement with the literature does not settle it. Adamatzky and Jones report 1–2 min at 2–3 mV with this electrode geometry. An interface artifact common to that geometry would produce the same agreement.

Framing

Why an organism and a language model

Neither system has a part inside it that is in charge. Physarum is one cell with no nervous system: different parts of it contract slightly out of step with each other, and the direction it moves is a consequence of that timing. A language model has no single place where meaning is stored. It is a large set of numbers, and every word it produces comes from all of them at once.

Where they differ is what the relations hold between. The organism's are in the physical world and are between places: a network of tubes, food, the lag from one electrode to the next. The model's are held inside memory, as vectors. So the electrodes flatten an arrangement in space into a sequence of numbers, and the light array turns a sequence back into an arrangement in space.

In the closed form of the work, a reduction layer turns half an hour of recording into four quantities: period, amplitude, the phase lag between electrodes, and baseline drift, and hands them to a language model running locally. The model has one action: it can illuminate one of nine regions of the chamber. It is never told whether the action had any effect. That loop has run: 464 turns over 12 days, 6–22 August 2026, all on the BLIND prompt, logged to data/logs/turns_*.jsonl. What it has not yet done is run against a colonized electrode. Every one of those turns predates the first bridge on 24 August, so the model has never been coupled to a live signal.

It does not translate. There is no dictionary between the organism's electrical activity and natural language. I built the layer that refuses to report anything it cannot distinguish from noise before I built anything else.

The asymmetry is deliberate and is not resolved by pretending otherwise. Physarum registers blue and UV light, chemical gradients, humidity, temperature, contact, and the stiffness of what it sits on. It has no receptor for a language model. It can be shaped by one, but it has no way of registering that one exists. The model receives the organism as four numbers. Two systems can still entrain each other without either knowing anything about the other. The earth entrains the moon, and the moon the tides.

No claim of understanding the organism is being made, because it is not available. This is not interpretation and not speaking for it: it is sampling it up into the band of human perception and presenting that, which is what places the work in art rather than science. Scientific practice is borrowed where it is needed: designing the controls, measuring the noise floor, and the refusal to report what cannot be told from noise.

Method, in order steps 5 → 9
as recorded

How the record was kept

The recording protocol is a numbered sequence, and the numbers are real: each step had to finish before the next could mean anything.

  • 5 · Noise floor, no organism. The pre-connection window of run 6 served as the blank. Per-sample noise 0.02–0.10 mV, against 0.7–2.8 mV before the converter's data rate was corrected on 2026-08-22.
  • 6 · Organism in. 2026-08-24 to 08-26, 50 hours continuous. Two probes reached, 10.7 h and 20.6 h after inoculation. The 2.2–2.4 min oscillation on both.
  • 7 · Organism removed. Same dish, fresh agar. Pre-registered in writing before any of its data was read, including the threshold that would have called the whole thing an artifact. 14 hours analyzed, 0 crossed it.
  • 8 · Organism returned to the same blocks. The line came back, on the channel run 6 had used as its never-colonized control.
  • 9 · Blue light, organism in place. Pre-registered 2026-09-06, amended 2026-09-08, never run. Blocked on the light panel.

Controls that were run and passed

  • Chamber temperature and humidity carry their own rhythm at 4.00 min, at 0.0027 °C and 0.0008 % RH. Nothing at 2.4 min.
  • The camera fires every 300 s. No 300 s line appears in the recording; 132 captures epoch-averaged give a largest excursion of z = 2.7 over 301 lags.
  • The rhythm survives subtracting one channel from another, so it is not coming in through the shared reference.
  • The large slow voltage swing after each connection is the connection settling, not the room: it correlates with chamber temperature at r = 0.04.

A filtered trace is not evidence. A filtered trace, plotted after narrowing the recording to 90–200 s, will look convincingly rhythmic for any input at all, including pure noise. Every number on this page compares against a reference instead: neighboring speeds, or the same electrode's own earlier hours.

Where it stands 2026-09-12

The dish today

No tube has formed this week. A strong sclerotium, the dormant, dried-down state the organism can hold for months, is in the dish, and whether it revives into a plasmodium and puts out a tube decides what happens next.

Nothing downstream can proceed without a tube. The light-stimulus run needs a connected electrode. So does running the loop against a live signal, which it has not done yet.

The summer produced a working rig, a recording method with its controls run and written down in advance, 464 turns of the model loop, and one result: a 2.2–2.4 minute oscillation that appears only where the organism has reached an electrode. What it did not produce is a test that says whether that oscillation is the organism itself.

What comes next experiments
paper
instruments

Three directions, in dependency order

1 · The experiments

  • Fix the condensation, then run the blue-light test. Organism connected, blue on for an hour and off for an hour, six pairs. If the rhythm is the organism, light should change it; surface chemistry has no reason to. The protocol, statistic, decision rule and void conditions are already written down and locked.
  • Run it on more than one dish. Everything in this document comes from a single dish and a single organism.
  • Run the loop against a live signal. The model drives the panel with a tube connected, so light events and a live signal exist in the same hours for the first time. Until then the entrainment question has not been tested.

2 · The paper

A method paper rather than a claim about slime moulds. The question it takes on: what evidence standard should hold when a language model is looped with a system that cannot be interrogated, one that has no way of reporting what it did or why, and no receptor for the model at all. The apparatus described here is the worked example, and the refusal to report anything indistinguishable from noise is the contribution.

3 · The instruments

The organism's architecture as a design for signal processing.

Further experimentation with different prompts, giving the model a way to reward the slime with food, and developing software and hardware based patches and effects for music.

The summer's work will also be written up as a paper, to be published in a book of other slime mould explorations sometime in 2028.

The organism has no central clock, and its behavior falls out of the phase relations between patches that each contract on their own rhythm, a bank of coupled oscillators with no master. So coupling strength is the control rather than pitch: coherent, and the bank locks and holds nearly still; lags drift, and it comes apart into beating before re-locking somewhere new.

Coupled nonlinear oscillators mode-lock at small-integer ratios and the locking region narrows as the integers grow, so simple ratios hold and complicated ones barely do. The tuning is just intonation because that is what the circuit already does, not because it was imposed on it.
